Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (<15%) is internally inconsistent with its own cited source, which reported 22.4% for 2023 -- a figure that itself falls in the 15-29% band. World Bank/ITU data (IT.NET.USER.ZS, sourced via FRED) puts individuals using the internet in Niger at 15.6% in 2024, up from 13.1% in 2022 and 13.0% in 2023. DataReportal/Kepios modelled estimates run higher, at 16.9% (Jan 2024) and 23.2% (Jan 2025). Both independent series place Niger above the 15% threshold, so the value code moves from 1 to 2 (15-29%).
revised_comments: World Bank/ITU data put individuals using the internet in Niger at 15.6% in 2024, having risen from around 13% in 2022-2023. DataReportal's Kepios-modelled estimate for early 2025 is higher, at 23.2%, corroborating a mid-teens-to-low-twenties internet penetration rate.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank SDG7 tracking data (via Tracking SDG7/ESMAP, cross-checked with Trading Economics) shows 20.1% national electricity access in 2023, the latest year available in the World Bank series as of mid-2026. This sits well within the <25% band, so the value code of 1 is retained.
revised_comments: World Bank Tracking SDG7 data show national electricity access in Niger at 20.1% of the population in 2023, the most recent year for which official data are available.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: The original comment correctly records urban access at 67.4% and rural access at 10.4% (World Bank, 2023), but 67.4-10.4 = 57 percentage points, which the scale places in the 41-60pp band (code 2), not the >60pp band (code 1) that was actually assigned. Figures re-verified directly against World Bank data via Trading Economics and cross-checked against Tracking SDG7/ESMAP, which confirms 2023 as the latest available year. Value code corrected from 1 to 2 to match the scale definition.
revised_comments: World Bank data for 2023 show electricity access at 67.4% of the urban population against 10.4% of the rural population in Niger, an urban-rural gap of 57 percentage points.
